plain: Periods are absent: missed for 3 or more months, or never started.
Infrequent periods, with cycles longer than 35 days.
Painful periods.
Very heavy or long-lasting periods.
Bleeding between periods.
The very first period in a girl's life.
When an ovary releases an egg, usually around the middle of the cycle.
The inner lining of the uterus (womb). It builds up each month and sheds during a period.
The second half of the cycle, after ovulation and before the next period.
A common hormone condition. It can cause irregular periods, acne, extra hair growth, and small follicles (cyst-like) on the ovaries.
Tissue like the womb lining grows outside the womb, often causing pain and sometimes trouble getting pregnant.
A non-cancerous growth in the wall of the womb. Many cause no problem; some cause heavy bleeding or pain.
A fluid-filled sac on an ovary. Most are harmless and go away on their own.
The thyroid gland makes too little hormone. It can cause tiredness, weight gain, and feeling cold.
The thyroid gland makes too much hormone. It can cause weight loss, fast heartbeat, and sweating.
Low hemoglobin: the blood carries less oxygen. Often causes tiredness and breathlessness.
Not enough iron in the body, the most common cause of anemia in women.
Higher than usual prolactin hormone. It can stop periods or cause milk discharge when not pregnant.
The body does not respond well to insulin, so blood sugar can rise. Common with PCOS.
Extra dark hair growth on the face, chest or belly, often linked to high male-type hormones.
Bones become weak and break easily. Risk rises after menopause.
An infection of the bladder or urine passage, causing burning while passing urine.
When periods have stopped for 12 months in a row, usually between ages 45 and 55.
The years before menopause when periods and hormones start to change.
High blood sugar that is first found during pregnancy.
High blood pressure with other warning signs in pregnancy. Needs urgent medical care.
High blood pressure.
One of the three 3-month stages of pregnancy.
A pregnancy that grows outside the womb. It is an emergency.
Loss of a pregnancy early on, before 20 weeks.
Care given during pregnancy, before the baby is born.
The number of times a woman has been pregnant.
Making breast milk after childbirth.
A low-dose X-ray of the breast used to find changes early.
A screening test that checks the cervix for abnormal cells.
Human papillomavirus, a common virus that causes most cervical cancers if it stays for years.
A tiny tissue sample taken and examined in a lab.
A scan that uses sound waves to see inside the body. No radiation.
Not cancer.
Cancer. Needs quick specialist care.
The protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen. Low value means anemia.
Thyroid-stimulating hormone. Tells how well the thyroid is working.
Average blood sugar over the last 2 to 3 months.
Blood sugar measured after at least 8 hours without food.
Shows how much iron is stored in the body.
A hormone that helps make breast milk. High levels can stop periods.
A vitamin that keeps bones strong. Low levels are very common.
A vitamin needed for blood and nerves. Low levels cause tiredness and tingling.
A fat in the blood. High levels raise the risk of heart disease.
Male-type hormones that women also make in small amounts.
The main female hormone. It controls periods and protects bones.
A hormone that prepares the womb for pregnancy.
Follicle-stimulating hormone. Helps eggs mature in the ovary.
An operation to remove the womb.
Body mass index, a number from height and weight.
